controls.description: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in sequential step order and without skipping steps.
controls.title: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in sequential step order and without skipping steps.

controls.description: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows with all steps being processed in realistic human time, i.e. transactions are not submitted too quickly.
controls.title: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows with all steps being processed in realistic human time, i.e. transactions are not submitted too quickly.

controls.description: Verify the application has appropriate limits for specific business actions or transactions which are correctly enforced on a per user basis.
controls.title: Verify the application has appropriate limits for specific business actions or transactions which are correctly enforced on a per user basis.

controls.description: Verify that the application has anti-automation controls to protect against excessive calls such as mass data exfiltration, business logic requests, file uploads or denial of service attacks.
controls.title: Verify that the application has anti-automation controls to protect against excessive calls such as mass data exfiltration, business logic requests, file uploads or denial of service attacks.

controls.description: Verify the application has business logic limits or validation to protect against likely business risks or threats, identified using threat modeling or similar methodologies.
controls.title: Verify the application has business logic limits or validation to protect against likely business risks or threats, identified using threat modeling or similar methodologies.

controls.description: Verify that the application does not suffer from "Time Of Check to Time Of Use" (TOCTOU) issues or other race conditions for sensitive operations.
controls.title: Verify that the application does not suffer from "Time Of Check to Time Of Use" (TOCTOU) issues or other race conditions for sensitive operations.

controls.description: Verify that the application monitors for unusual events or activity from a business logic perspective. For example, attempts to perform actions out of order or actions which a normal user would never attempt.
controls.title: Verify that the application monitors for unusual events or activity from a business logic perspective. For example, attempts to perform actions out of order or actions which a normal user would never attempt.

controls.description: Verify that the application has configurable alerting when automated attacks or unusual activity is detected.
controls.title: Verify that the application has configurable alerting when automated attacks or unusual activity is detected.

controls.description: Verify that the application will not accept large files that could fill up storage or cause a denial of service.
controls.title: Verify that the application will not accept large files that could fill up storage or cause a denial of service.

controls.description: Verify that the application checks compressed files (e.g. zip, gz, docx, odt) against maximum allowed uncompressed size and against maximum number of files before uncompressing the file.
controls.title: Verify that the application checks compressed files (e.g. zip, gz, docx, odt) against maximum allowed uncompressed size and against maximum number of files before uncompressing the file.

controls.description: Verify that a file size quota and maximum number of files per user is enforced to ensure that a single user cannot fill up the storage with too many files, or excessively large files.
controls.title: Verify that a file size quota and maximum number of files per user is enforced to ensure that a single user cannot fill up the storage with too many files, or excessively large files.

controls.description: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are validated to be of expected type based on the file's content.
controls.title: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are validated to be of expected type based on the file's content.

controls.description: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is not used directly by system or framework filesystems and that a URL API is used to protect against path traversal.
controls.title: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is not used directly by system or framework filesystems and that a URL API is used to protect against path traversal.

controls.description: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is validated or ignored to prevent the disclosure, creation, updating or removal of local files (LFI).
controls.title: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is validated or ignored to prevent the disclosure, creation, updating or removal of local files (LFI).

controls.description: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is validated or ignored to prevent the disclosure or execution of remote files via Remote File Inclusion (RFI) or Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.
controls.title: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is validated or ignored to prevent the disclosure or execution of remote files via Remote File Inclusion (RFI) or Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

controls.description: Verify that the application protects against Reflective File Download (RFD) by validating or ignoring user-submitted filenames in a JSON, JSONP, or URL parameter, the response Content-Type header should be set to text/plain, and the Content-Disposition header should have a fixed filename.
controls.title: Verify that the application protects against Reflective File Download (RFD) by validating or ignoring user-submitted filenames in a JSON, JSONP, or URL parameter, the response Content-Type header should be set to text/plain, and the Content-Disposition header should have a fixed filename.

controls.description: Verify that untrusted file metadata is not used directly with system API or libraries, to protect against OS command injection.
controls.title: Verify that untrusted file metadata is not used directly with system API or libraries, to protect against OS command injection.

controls.description: Verify that the application does not include and execute functionality from untrusted sources, such as unverified content distribution networks, JavaScript libraries, node npm libraries, or server-side DLLs.
controls.title: Verify that the application does not include and execute functionality from untrusted sources, such as unverified content distribution networks, JavaScript libraries, node npm libraries, or server-side DLLs.

controls.description: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are stored outside the web root, with limited permissions.
controls.title: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are stored outside the web root, with limited permissions.

controls.description: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are scanned by antivirus scanners to prevent upload and serving of known malicious content.
controls.title: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are scanned by antivirus scanners to prevent upload and serving of known malicious content.

controls.description: Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information and source code leakage. For example, backup files (e.g. .bak), temporary working files (e.g. .swp), compressed files (.zip, .tar.gz, etc) and other extensions commonly used by editors should be blocked unless required.
controls.title: Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information and source code leakage. For example, backup files (e.g. .bak), temporary working files (e.g. .swp), compressed files (.zip, .tar.gz, etc) and other extensions commonly used by editors should be blocked unless required.

controls.description: Verify that direct requests to uploaded files will never be executed as HTML/JavaScript content.
controls.title: Verify that direct requests to uploaded files will never be executed as HTML/JavaScript content.

controls.description: Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allow list of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data/files from.
controls.title: Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allow list of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data/files from.

controls.description: Verify that all application components use the same encodings and parsers to avoid parsing attacks that exploit different URI or file parsing behavior that could be used in SSRF and RFI attacks.
controls.title: Verify that all application components use the same encodings and parsers to avoid parsing attacks that exploit different URI or file parsing behavior that could be used in SSRF and RFI attacks.

controls.description: Verify API URLs do not expose sensitive information, such as the API key, session tokens etc.
controls.title: Verify API URLs do not expose sensitive information, such as the API key, session tokens etc.

controls.description: Verify that authorization decisions are made at both the URI, enforced by programmatic or declarative security at the controller or router, and at the resource level, enforced by model-based permissions.
controls.title: Verify that authorization decisions are made at both the URI, enforced by programmatic or declarative security at the controller or router, and at the resource level, enforced by model-based permissions.

controls.description: Verify that requests containing unexpected or missing content types are rejected with appropriate headers (HTTP response status 406 Unacceptable or 415 Unsupported Media Type).
controls.title: Verify that requests containing unexpected or missing content types are rejected with appropriate headers (HTTP response status 406 Unacceptable or 415 Unsupported Media Type).

controls.description: Verify that enabled RESTful HTTP methods are a valid choice for the user or action, such as preventing normal users using DELETE or PUT on protected API or resources.
controls.title: Verify that enabled RESTful HTTP methods are a valid choice for the user or action, such as preventing normal users using DELETE or PUT on protected API or resources.

controls.description: Verify that JSON schema validation is in place and verified before accepting input.
controls.title: Verify that JSON schema validation is in place and verified before accepting input.

controls.description: Verify that RESTful web services that utilize cookies are protected from Cross-Site Request Forgery via the use of at least one or more of the following: double submit cookie pattern, CSRF nonces, or Origin request header checks.
controls.title: Verify that RESTful web services that utilize cookies are protected from Cross-Site Request Forgery via the use of at least one or more of the following: double submit cookie pattern, CSRF nonces, or Origin request header checks.

controls.description: Verify that REST services explicitly check the incoming Content-Type to be the expected one, such as application/xml or application/json.
controls.title: Verify that REST services explicitly check the incoming Content-Type to be the expected one, such as application/xml or application/json.

controls.description: Verify that the message headers and payload are trustworthy and not modified in transit. Requiring strong encryption for transport (TLS only) may be sufficient in many cases as it provides both confidentiality and integrity protection. Per-message digital signatures can provide additional assurance on top of the transport protections for high-security applications but bring with them additional complexity and risks to weigh against the benefits.
controls.title: Verify that the message headers and payload are trustworthy and not modified in transit. Requiring strong encryption for transport (TLS only) may be sufficient in many cases as it provides both confidentiality and integrity protection. Per-message digital signatures can provide additional assurance on top of the transport protections for high-security applications but bring with them additional complexity and risks to weigh against the benefits.

controls.description: Verify that XSD schema validation takes place to ensure a properly formed XML document, followed by validation of each input field before any processing of that data takes place.
controls.title: Verify that XSD schema validation takes place to ensure a properly formed XML document, followed by validation of each input field before any processing of that data takes place.

controls.description: Verify that the message payload is signed using WS-Security to ensure reliable transport between client and service.
controls.title: Verify that the message payload is signed using WS-Security to ensure reliable transport between client and service.

controls.description: Verify that a query allow list or a combination of depth limiting and amount limiting is used to prevent GraphQL or data layer expression Denial of Service (DoS) as a result of expensive, nested queries. For more advanced scenarios, query cost analysis should be used.
controls.title: Verify that a query allow list or a combination of depth limiting and amount limiting is used to prevent GraphQL or data layer expression Denial of Service (DoS) as a result of expensive, nested queries. For more advanced scenarios, query cost analysis should be used.

controls.description: Verify that GraphQL or other data layer authorization logic should be implemented at the business logic layer instead of the GraphQL layer.
controls.title: Verify that GraphQL or other data layer authorization logic should be implemented at the business logic layer instead of the GraphQL layer.

controls.description: Verify that the application build and deployment processes are performed in a secure and repeatable way, such as CI / CD automation, automated configuration management, and automated deployment scripts.
controls.title: Verify that the application build and deployment processes are performed in a secure and repeatable way, such as CI / CD automation, automated configuration management, and automated deployment scripts.

controls.description: Verify that compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found.
controls.title: Verify that compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found.

controls.description: Verify that server configuration is hardened as per the recommendations of the application server and frameworks in use.
controls.title: Verify that server configuration is hardened as per the recommendations of the application server and frameworks in use.

controls.description: Verify that the application, configuration, and all dependencies can be re-deployed using automated deployment scripts, built from a documented and tested runbook in a reasonable time, or restored from backups in a timely fashion.
controls.title: Verify that the application, configuration, and all dependencies can be re-deployed using automated deployment scripts, built from a documented and tested runbook in a reasonable time, or restored from backups in a timely fashion.

controls.description: Verify that authorized administrators can verify the integrity of all security-relevant configurations to detect tampering.
controls.title: Verify that authorized administrators can verify the integrity of all security-relevant configurations to detect tampering.

controls.description: Verify that all components are up to date, preferably using a dependency checker during build or compile time.
controls.title: Verify that all components are up to date, preferably using a dependency checker during build or compile time.

controls.description: Verify that all unneeded features, documentation, sample applications and configurations are removed.
controls.title: Verify that all unneeded features, documentation, sample applications and configurations are removed.

controls.description: Verify that if application assets, such as JavaScript libraries, CSS or web fonts, are hosted externally on a Content Delivery Network (CDN) or external provider, Subresource Integrity (SRI) is used to validate the integrity of the asset.
controls.title: Verify that if application assets, such as JavaScript libraries, CSS or web fonts, are hosted externally on a Content Delivery Network (CDN) or external provider, Subresource Integrity (SRI) is used to validate the integrity of the asset.

controls.description: Verify that third party components come from pre-defined, trusted and continually maintained repositories.
controls.title: Verify that third party components come from pre-defined, trusted and continually maintained repositories.

controls.description: Verify that a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is maintained of all third party libraries in use.
controls.title: Verify that a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is maintained of all third party libraries in use.

controls.description: Verify that the attack surface is reduced by sandboxing or encapsulating third party libraries to expose only the required behaviour into the application.
controls.title: Verify that the attack surface is reduced by sandboxing or encapsulating third party libraries to expose only the required behaviour into the application.

controls.description: Verify that web or application server and application framework debug modes are disabled in production to eliminate debug features, developer consoles, and unintended security disclosures.
controls.title: Verify that web or application server and application framework debug modes are disabled in production to eliminate debug features, developer consoles, and unintended security disclosures.

controls.description: Verify that the HTTP headers or any part of the HTTP response do not expose detailed version information of system components.
controls.title: Verify that the HTTP headers or any part of the HTTP response do not expose detailed version information of system components.

controls.description: Verify that every HTTP response contains a Content-Type header. Also specify a safe character set (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) if the content types are text/*, /+xml and application/xml. Content must match with the provided Content-Type header.
controls.title: Verify that every HTTP response contains a Content-Type header. Also specify a safe character set (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) if the content types are text/*, /+xml and application/xml. Content must match with the provided Content-Type header.

controls.description: Verify that all API responses contain a Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="api.json" header (or other appropriate filename for the content type).
controls.title: Verify that all API responses contain a Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="api.json" header (or other appropriate filename for the content type).

controls.description: Verify that a Content Security Policy (CSP) response header is in place that helps mitigate impact for XSS attacks like HTML, DOM, JSON, and JavaScript injection vulnerabilities.
controls.title: Verify that a Content Security Policy (CSP) response header is in place that helps mitigate impact for XSS attacks like HTML, DOM, JSON, and JavaScript injection vulnerabilities.

controls.description: Verify that all responses contain a X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header.
controls.title: Verify that all responses contain a X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header.

controls.description: Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header is included on all responses and for all subdomains, such as Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15724800; includeSubdomains.
controls.title: Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header is included on all responses and for all subdomains, such as Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15724800; includeSubdomains.

controls.description: Verify that a suitable Referrer-Policy header is included to avoid exposing sensitive information in the URL through the Referer header to untrusted parties.
controls.title: Verify that a suitable Referrer-Policy header is included to avoid exposing sensitive information in the URL through the Referer header to untrusted parties.

controls.description: Verify that the content of a web application cannot be embedded in a third-party site by default and that embedding of the exact resources is only allowed where necessary by using suitable Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options response headers.
controls.title: Verify that the content of a web application cannot be embedded in a third-party site by default and that embedding of the exact resources is only allowed where necessary by using suitable Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options response headers.

controls.description: Verify that the application server only accepts the HTTP methods in use by the application/API, including pre-flight OPTIONS, and logs/alerts on any requests that are not valid for the application context.
controls.title: Verify that the application server only accepts the HTTP methods in use by the application/API, including pre-flight OPTIONS, and logs/alerts on any requests that are not valid for the application context.

controls.description: Verify that the supplied Origin header is not used for authentication or access control decisions, as the Origin header can easily be changed by an attacker.
controls.title: Verify that the supplied Origin header is not used for authentication or access control decisions, as the Origin header can easily be changed by an attacker.

controls.description: Verify that the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Access-Control-Allow-Origin header uses a strict allow list of trusted domains and subdomains to match against and does not support the "null" origin.
controls.title: Verify that the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Access-Control-Allow-Origin header uses a strict allow list of trusted domains and subdomains to match against and does not support the "null" origin.

controls.description: Verify that HTTP headers added by a trusted proxy or SSO devices, such as a bearer token, are authenticated by the application.
controls.title: Verify that HTTP headers added by a trusted proxy or SSO devices, such as a bearer token, are authenticated by the application.

controls.description: Verify that user set passwords are at least 12 characters in length (after multiple spaces are combined).
controls.title: Verify that user set passwords are at least 12 characters in length (after multiple spaces are combined).

controls.description: Verify that there are no periodic credential rotation or password history requirements.
controls.title: Verify that there are no periodic credential rotation or password history requirements.

controls.description: Verify that "paste" functionality, browser password helpers, and external password managers are permitted.
controls.title: Verify that "paste" functionality, browser password helpers, and external password managers are permitted.

controls.description: Verify that the user can choose to either temporarily view the entire masked password, or temporarily view the last typed character of the password on platforms that do not have this as built-in functionality.
controls.title: Verify that the user can choose to either temporarily view the entire masked password, or temporarily view the last typed character of the password on platforms that do not have this as built-in functionality.

controls.description: Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted, and that passwords of more than 128 characters are denied.
controls.title: Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted, and that passwords of more than 128 characters are denied.

controls.description: Verify that password truncation is not performed. However, consecutive multiple spaces may be replaced by a single space.
controls.title: Verify that password truncation is not performed. However, consecutive multiple spaces may be replaced by a single space.

controls.description: Verify that any printable Unicode character, including language neutral characters such as spaces and Emojis are permitted in passwords.
controls.title: Verify that any printable Unicode character, including language neutral characters such as spaces and Emojis are permitted in passwords.

controls.description: Verify users can change their password.
controls.title: Verify users can change their password.

controls.description: Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password.
controls.title: Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password.

controls.description: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration, login, and password change are checked against a set of breached passwords either locally (such as the top 1,000 or 10,000 most common passwords which match the system's password policy) or using an external API. If using an API a zero knowledge proof or other mechanism should be used to ensure that the plain text password is not sent or used in verifying the breach status of the password. If the password is breached, the application must require the user to set a new non-breached password. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))
controls.title: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration, login, and password change are checked against a set of breached passwords either locally (such as the top 1,000 or 10,000 most common passwords which match the system's password policy) or using an external API. If using an API a zero knowledge proof or other mechanism should be used to ensure that the plain text password is not sent or used in verifying the breach status of the password. If the password is breached, the application must require the user to set a new non-breached password. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

controls.description: Verify that a password strength meter is provided to help users set a stronger password.
controls.title: Verify that a password strength meter is provided to help users set a stronger password.

controls.description: Verify that there are no password composition rules limiting the type of characters permitted. There should be no requirement for upper or lower case or numbers or special characters.
controls.title: Verify that there are no password composition rules limiting the type of characters permitted. There should be no requirement for upper or lower case or numbers or special characters.

controls.description: Verify that intra-service secrets do not rely on unchanging credentials such as passwords, API keys or shared accounts with privileged access.
controls.title: Verify that intra-service secrets do not rely on unchanging credentials such as passwords, API keys or shared accounts with privileged access.

controls.description: Verify that if passwords are required for service authentication, the service account used is not a default credential. (e.g. root/root or admin/admin are default in some services during installation).
controls.title: Verify that if passwords are required for service authentication, the service account used is not a default credential. (e.g. root/root or admin/admin are default in some services during installation).

controls.description: Verify that passwords are stored with sufficient protection to prevent offline recovery attacks, including local system access.
controls.title: Verify that passwords are stored with sufficient protection to prevent offline recovery attacks, including local system access.

controls.description: Verify passwords, integrations with databases and third-party systems, seeds and internal secrets, and API keys are managed securely and not included in the source code or stored within source code repositories. Such storage SHOULD resist offline attacks. The use of a secure software key store (L1), hardware TPM, or an HSM (L3) is recommended for password storage.
controls.title: Verify passwords, integrations with databases and third-party systems, seeds and internal secrets, and API keys are managed securely and not included in the source code or stored within source code repositories. Such storage SHOULD resist offline attacks. The use of a secure software key store (L1), hardware TPM, or an HSM (L3) is recommended for password storage.

controls.description: Verify that anti-automation controls are effective at mitigating breached credential testing, brute force, and account lockout attacks. Such controls include blocking the most common breached passwords, soft lockouts, rate limiting, CAPTCHA, ever increasing delays between attempts, IP address restrictions, or risk-based restrictions such as location, first login on a device, recent attempts to unlock the account, or similar. Verify that no more than 100 failed attempts per hour is possible on a single account.
controls.title: Verify that anti-automation controls are effective at mitigating breached credential testing, brute force, and account lockout attacks. Such controls include blocking the most common breached passwords, soft lockouts, rate limiting, CAPTCHA, ever increasing delays between attempts, IP address restrictions, or risk-based restrictions such as location, first login on a device, recent attempts to unlock the account, or similar. Verify that no more than 100 failed attempts per hour is possible on a single account.

controls.description: Verify that the use of weak authenticators (such as SMS and email) is limited to secondary verification and transaction approval and not as a replacement for more secure authentication methods. Verify that stronger methods are offered before weak methods, users are aware of the risks, or that proper measures are in place to limit the risks of account compromise.
controls.title: Verify that the use of weak authenticators (such as SMS and email) is limited to secondary verification and transaction approval and not as a replacement for more secure authentication methods. Verify that stronger methods are offered before weak methods, users are aware of the risks, or that proper measures are in place to limit the risks of account compromise.

controls.description: Verify that secure notifications are sent to users after updates to authentication details, such as credential resets, email or address changes, logging in from unknown or risky locations. The use of push notifications - rather than SMS or email - is preferred, but in the absence of push notifications, SMS or email is acceptable as long as no sensitive information is disclosed in the notification.
controls.title: Verify that secure notifications are sent to users after updates to authentication details, such as credential resets, email or address changes, logging in from unknown or risky locations. The use of push notifications - rather than SMS or email - is preferred, but in the absence of push notifications, SMS or email is acceptable as long as no sensitive information is disclosed in the notification.

controls.description: Verify impersonation resistance against phishing, such as the use of multi-factor authentication, cryptographic devices with intent (such as connected keys with a push to authenticate), or at higher AAL levels, client-side certificates.
controls.title: Verify impersonation resistance against phishing, such as the use of multi-factor authentication, cryptographic devices with intent (such as connected keys with a push to authenticate), or at higher AAL levels, client-side certificates.

controls.description: Verify that where a Credential Service Provider (CSP) and the application verifying authentication are separated, mutually authenticated TLS is in place between the two endpoints.
controls.title: Verify that where a Credential Service Provider (CSP) and the application verifying authentication are separated, mutually authenticated TLS is in place between the two endpoints.

controls.description: Verify replay resistance through the mandated use of One-time Passwords (OTP) devices, cryptographic authenticators, or lookup codes.
controls.title: Verify replay resistance through the mandated use of One-time Passwords (OTP) devices, cryptographic authenticators, or lookup codes.

controls.description: Verify intent to authenticate by requiring the entry of an OTP token or user-initiated action such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key.
controls.title: Verify intent to authenticate by requiring the entry of an OTP token or user-initiated action such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key.

controls.description: Verify system generated initial passwords or activation codes SHOULD be securely randomly generated, SHOULD be at least 6 characters long, and MAY contain letters and numbers, and expire after a short period of time. These initial secrets must not be permitted to become the long term password.
controls.title: Verify system generated initial passwords or activation codes SHOULD be securely randomly generated, SHOULD be at least 6 characters long, and MAY contain letters and numbers, and expire after a short period of time. These initial secrets must not be permitted to become the long term password.

controls.description: Verify that enrollment and use of user-provided authentication devices are supported, such as a U2F or FIDO tokens.
controls.title: Verify that enrollment and use of user-provided authentication devices are supported, such as a U2F or FIDO tokens.

controls.description: Verify that renewal instructions are sent with sufficient time to renew time bound authenticators.
controls.title: Verify that renewal instructions are sent with sufficient time to renew time bound authenticators.

controls.description: Verify that passwords are stored in a form that is resistant to offline attacks. Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using an approved one-way key derivation or password hashing function. Key derivation and password hashing functions take a password, a salt, and a cost factor as inputs when generating a password hash.
controls.title: Verify that passwords are stored in a form that is resistant to offline attacks. Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using an approved one-way key derivation or password hashing function. Key derivation and password hashing functions take a password, a salt, and a cost factor as inputs when generating a password hash.

controls.description: Verify that the salt is at least 32 bits in length and be chosen arbitrarily to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes. For each credential, a unique salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored.
controls.title: Verify that the salt is at least 32 bits in length and be chosen arbitrarily to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes. For each credential, a unique salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored.

controls.description: Verify that if PBKDF2 is used, the iteration count SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, typically at least 100,000 iterations.
controls.title: Verify that if PBKDF2 is used, the iteration count SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, typically at least 100,000 iterations.

controls.description: Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, with a minimum of 10.
controls.title: Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, with a minimum of 10.

controls.description: Verify that an additional iteration of a key derivation function is performed, using a salt value that is secret and known only to the verifier. Generate the salt value using an approved random bit generator [SP 800-90Ar1] and provide at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of SP 800-131A. The secret salt value SHALL be stored separately from the hashed passwords (e.g., in a specialized device like a hardware security module).
controls.title: Verify that an additional iteration of a key derivation function is performed, using a salt value that is secret and known only to the verifier. Generate the salt value using an approved random bit generator [SP 800-90Ar1] and provide at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of SP 800-131A. The secret salt value SHALL be stored separately from the hashed passwords (e.g., in a specialized device like a hardware security module).

controls.description: Verify that a system generated initial activation or recovery secret is not sent in clear text to the user.
controls.title: Verify that a system generated initial activation or recovery secret is not sent in clear text to the user.

controls.description: Verify password hints or knowledge-based authentication (so-called "secret questions") are not present.
controls.title: Verify password hints or knowledge-based authentication (so-called "secret questions") are not present.

controls.description: Verify password credential recovery does not reveal the current password in any way.
controls.title: Verify password credential recovery does not reveal the current password in any way.

controls.description: Verify shared or default accounts are not present (e.g. "root", "admin", or "sa").
controls.title: Verify shared or default accounts are not present (e.g. "root", "admin", or "sa").

controls.description: Verify that if an authentication factor is changed or replaced, that the user is notified of this event.
controls.title: Verify that if an authentication factor is changed or replaced, that the user is notified of this event.

controls.description: Verify forgotten password, and other recovery paths use a secure recovery mechanism, such as time-based OTP (TOTP) or other soft token, mobile push, or another offline recovery mechanism.
controls.title: Verify forgotten password, and other recovery paths use a secure recovery mechanism, such as time-based OTP (TOTP) or other soft token, mobile push, or another offline recovery mechanism.
